messages:
alex: customer reports intermittent 500s and spikes to 2-3s tail latency on Dedicated cluster eu-west-1. They included a couple request ids but asked us to gather logs to repro.
customer-ops: pasted customer's snippet: \"curl -i https://api.redwood-inference.com/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer ...' -d '{\\\"model\\\":\\\"rwd-7b\\\", \\\"prompt\\\":\\\"hi\\\"}'\" and they said X-Request-ID: req_8a9f2 in their proxy logs.
sarah: can you ask them for a curl with the X-Request-ID header, full -v output, and exact body? we need exact bytes to reproduce. Also confirm the tenant id and which dedicated pool.
alex: asked. Customer replied: cluster rwd-dedicated-eu-west-1, pool gpu-a100-1. They sent this curl (token redacted) and the header X-Request-ID: req-1772500000-1. They see 502 / upstream read timeout in the gateway.
james: could be proxy timeout or worker OOM. We'll need pod logs, node dmesg, and GPU metrics for that window. Also exact timestamps for each request.
kyle: oncall note: when reproducing vs dedicated, include X-Tenant-ID: acct-1234 so traffic routes to their tenant.
deploy-bot: deploy rwd-dedicated-eu-west-1/gateway v1.46 promoted at 2026-03-10T02:11Z
alex: customer gave timestamps: 2026-03-15T14:03:22Z and 2026-03-15T14:08:10Z. I'll try to reproduce and ask them for full curl -v output (headers + body length).
sarah: if we need to pull logs from their node, ask for permission. We'll need to run: kubectl -n redwood logs gateway-<id> --since=1h and kubectl -n redwood logs worker-<id> --since=1h, plus node dmesg and nvidia-smi snapshots.
alex: provided commands I'll run (if approved):
  kubectl -n redwood logs gateway-abc --since=24h > /tmp/gw.log
  kubectl -n redwood logs worker-123 --since=24h > /tmp/worker.log
  sudo dmesg -T | tail -n 200 > /tmp/dmesg.txt
  nvidia-smi --query-gpu=utilization.gpu,temperature.gpu,memory.used --format=csv -lms 1000 -f /tmp/gpu.csv
  journalctl -u envoy -o short-iso --since \"2026-03-15 14:00:00\" --until \"2026-03-15 14:30:00\" > /tmp/envoy.log

james: also collect /var/log/kern.log and kubelet journal on the node, check for OOM kills. Look for kernel OOM messages around 14:03.
alex: customer approved remote fetch. I'm running the debug bundle tool now on the node: /opt/redwood/bin/debugbundle --request-ids req-1772500000-1,req-1772500000-2 --output /tmp/debug-reqs.tar.gz
alex: hitting permission error: \"cannot access /dev/nvidia0: permission denied\" when the debug tool probes nvml.
james: run with sudo; if the node is locked down, systemd-run or escalate to infra to allow nvml access.
alex: sudo fixed it. Bundle created /tmp/debug-reqs.tar.gz (~120MB). Uploading to internal support bucket.
alex: upload complete: https://s3.redwood-internal/acct-1234/1772500000-debug-reqs.tar.gz
sarah: pulling bundle now. Items to inspect: dmesg for OOM, worker core dumps, python traceback stacks, nvml logs, envoy timeouts, and any large heap growth in worker metrics. Search for \"upstream read timeout\" in gateway logs.
alex: gateway log excerpt pasted: 2026-03-15T14:03:22Z [WARN] upstream read timeout for req-1772500000-1, backend=worker-123, latency=30.003s
alex: worker log excerpt: 2026-03-15T14:03:21Z ERROR ModelInference error: KV cache memory pressure, failed allocate 1.2G
james: KV cache memory pressure explains long stalls — if the worker tried to allocate +1GB on GPU or host and hit memory limits it can stall or be OOM-killed. Query Prometheus for container_memory_usage_bytes{pod=\"worker-123\"} over that window and GPU exporter metrics.
kyle: also confirm model artifact: is this a quantized build? quantization + long prompts can inflate KV usage unexpectedly. Which model revision?
alex: model is rwd-7b-v2-q4_0 per customer request.
sarah: that matches the memory pressure hypothesis. Next steps: 1) collect exact prometheus timeseries for gpu memory and host memory, 2) check kernel OOM log lines in dmesg, 3) check for any worker restart loop or core dumps in the bundle.
james: I glanced at the bundle: kernel reports OOM kill for process model-worker pid=4521 at 2026-03-15T14:03:21, message: \"Out of memory: Killed process 4521 (python) total-vm: 12000000kB\"
kyle: that would generate 502s as gateway waits and backend disappears. Suggest short-term mitigation: reduce worker max_cache_entries and set worker GC thresholds, then restart affected worker pods sequentially to avoid mass eviction. Also consider isolating heavy tenant traffic.
alex: customer asked for a reproducible curl to show the 502. I reproduced it by sending a large prompt. Exact curl I used:
  curl -v \"https://dedicated.eu-west-1.redwood/api/v1/generate\" \\n    -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \\n    -H \"X-Request-ID: req-1772500000-1\" \\n    -H \"X-Tenant-ID: acct-1234\" \\n    -d '{"model":"rwd-7b-v2-q4_0","input":"<long prompt repeated 50k tokens>"}'
It returns 502 after ~30s with gateway log showing upstream timeout.
sarah: thanks. For remediation: a) hotfix to cap kv cache growth on quantized models, b) rolling worker restart with new config, c) add request throttling per-tenant to prevent single heavy prompt from exhausting worker memory. File tickets for runtime and infra.
james: created JIRA INF-3245 and attached the uploaded bundle + reproducer notes. P1. Assigned to eng-runtime.
alex: I've updated the customer with repro steps, shared the bundle link, and told them we're implementing mitigations. They want status updates every 12 hours.
kyle: additional checks: run nvidia-smi -q for ECC errors and nvlink peer errors, also check GPU driver logs in /var/log/nvidia-installer.log if present.
alex: noted, ran nvidia-smi --query and no ECC errors, but memory utilization spiked to 99% before OOM.
sarah: plan of record: patch config to limit kv cache (rollout today), schedule engine hotfix for memory leak (next week), and propose tenant-level rate limits. I'll own postmortem.
james: thanks team. If anything else suspicious in the bundle I'll ping.
alex: thanks all :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: incident created INF-3245 at 1772501000
